newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures end firm on first trading day.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures end firm on first trading day.

text.p: SIMEX MSCI Taiwan stock index futures finished firm on their first trading day on Thursday, but dealers said turnover was disappointingly low and futures did not track cash market movements.
"It was mainly complimentary trades. The market didn't really follow what the cash side was doing," said a trader with a local institution.

He said volumes were depressed by the absence of Taiwanese players and local interest was also hampered by the fact that the contract's trading time overlapped in part with trading of Nikkei 225 stock index futures.
The March contract on the MSCI Taiwan index ended at 307.3 against its opening 299.7 after hitting a high of 311.0. A mere 500 lots changed hands.

Taiwan has not yet legalised trading by local investors of the Taiwan stock index futures contracts launched on Thursday by both SIMEX and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) on the GLOBEX after-hours electronic trading system.
Traders said volatility on SIMEX had been low after the initial trades, driven mainly by some commission house and local dealer orders.
Dealers said they would need to monitor the performance of the contract over the next month to gauge the level of interest it was likely to attract.
On Wednesday, Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission urged local investors not to engage in "illegal" trading of Taiwan futures in Singapore and Chicago.
It said the law prohibited local futures brokerages from placing orders for Taiwan investors through overseas affiliates, and violators would be punished.
